line: Crowley’s Five of Wands: Strife, referred to Geburah, ruled also by Saturn and Leo.

sections.title: What Crowley names
sections.line: The chapter name for the card. The second quotation gives the element of its suit.

quotes.quote: the five of Wands is called Strife.
“Wands”, attributed to Fire; “Cups”, to Water; “Swords”, to Air;

sections.title: Its place on the Tree
sections.line: The card is referred to Geburah of the suit of Fire, and the tree essay gives Geburah as the sephira of a Five.

quotes.quote: This card is referred to Geburah of the suit of Fire.
and to the Sephira Geburah because it is a Five.

sections.title: What it figures
sections.line: Crowley’s account of the card’s fiery energy, the wand of the Chief Adept, and its volcanic scope.

quotes.quote: There is no limit to the scope of this volcanic energy.
The symbol represents the wand of the Chief Adept, showing that the authority is derived from the superiors;

sections.title: Conflicts and gaps
sections.line: The chapter text rules the card by Saturn and Leo. The attribution table (pdf 275, image only, not quoted) reads Saturn in Leo, and this page keeps the text reading.

quotes.quote: It is ruled also by Saturn and Leo.
It is also subject to the sign Leo, and to the planet Saturn, because this planet and sign determine the nature of the card.
